modelResponse.episodeSummary: Thomas B. Nguyen, 55M, Post-op day 1, Sinus rhythm with frequent PVCs/NSVT, warning severity, hemodynamically stable
modelResponse.rhythm: Sinus rhythm with frequent Premature Ventricular Contractions (PVCs), couplets, and a brief run of Non-Sustained Ventricular Tachycardia (NSVT)
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Sinus beats with multifocal wide PVCs, couplets, one non-sustained VT run of 4 beats
preEventNote: Post-op, on thiazide; PVC burden increasing over last hour
modelResponse.mechanism: Increased ventricular ectopy and potential for malignant arrhythmias due to electrolyte disturbances affecting cardiac myocyte repolarization and automaticity.

rejectedAlternatives.why: Troponin T 0.02 ng/mL is only mildly elevated and flagged as 'mild post-op', not indicative of acute ischemia. No significant ST deviation.
Patient is not on digoxin. No other medications listed are known to cause this type of arrhythmia.
While patient has mild diastolic dysfunction, the acute increase in ectopy and NSVT in the post-op setting with electrolyte abnormalities points away from this as the primary driver.

recommendedActions: Administer IV Magnesium Sulfate 2g over 5 minutes
Administer IV Potassium Chloride 20 mEq over 1 hour (monitor closely)
Consider telemetry if ectopy persists or worsens
Hold Hydrochlorothiazide until electrolytes are corrected
uncertainty: Exact cause of the NSVT run (electrolyte vs. other factors) is uncertain, but electrolyte imbalance is the most likely trigger.
Long-term implications of the ectopy are unknown.
